historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun's 'The Muqaddimah'. In this seminal work, Ibn Khaldun describes a Berber dynasty ruling in the Maghreb around the 13th century, known as the Marinids. The name 'Afraima' appears in connection with a sub-dynasty that reigned in the region of Tlemcen around 1286-1358. The term 'Afraima' may refer to the ruling family or to the capital city of Tlemcen.

Al-Maqrizi's 'The History of the Prophets and the Kings'. This 15th-century Egyptian historian describes the rule of the Hafsids in Tunisia (1236-1574). He mentions a Berber general named Ibn Abi Zara, who ruled over the eastern parts of the Hafsid dominions under the name 'Afraima'. The term 'Afraima' is believed to originate from the Berber word 'Afra', meaning 'white' or 'pure', and the Berber suffix '-im', indicating 'people of'. Thus, 'Afraima' may mean 'the people of the pure ones' or 'the people of the whites'.
